commands.author: steipete

target.title: fix(cron): stop a cron job's own marker from blocking its awaited wake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `wakeMode: "now"` main-session cron job installs its active execution marker before awaiting `runHeartbeatOnce`. The heartbeat admission guard then sees cron work in progress and can reject the wake that the job itself owns. The cron path falls back to an asynchronous request and records success before delivery is confirmed.

This is a deterministic defect found while investigating #105257. It fixes an adjacent, reproducible self-block; it does not claim to close that broader intermittent report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron path now passes its exact active marker `{ jobId, token }` through the internal Gateway heartbeat adapter. The heartbeat runner bypasses only that still-current marker:

- another cron job still blocks the wake;
- a same-ID replacement marker still blocks the stale owner;
- an absent or stale owner keeps the previous busy behavior;
- queued `cron.run` work cannot deadlock on its own `CommandLane.Cron` entry;
- the public plugin heartbeat facade cannot supply or forge internal ownership.

The exact token matters. Discounting by job ID alone would allow a superseded execution to claim ownership of a newer run.

## User Impact

Main-session `wakeMode: "now"` cron runs now wait for their owned heartbeat delivery before recording terminal success. Other cron work continues to enforce the existing admission fence. No config, storage, protocol, or public plugin API changes.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage exercises the full decision surface:

- exact marker, unrelated marker, same-ID replacement, and stale replacement;
- direct manual run, Gateway-queued `cron.run`, and natural scheduled firing;
- real heartbeat runner integration and Gateway adapter forwarding;
- owned Cron-lane pressure versus unowned busy behavior;
- marker and command-lane cleanup before sandbox deletion.

Results:

- 88 focused tests passed across cron active jobs, timer/service, Gateway adapter, and heartbeat runner.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on Blacksmith Testbox ([run 29629429145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29629429145)).
- Fresh autoreview found no actionable issue.

Live proof used the official OpenAI API with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, an isolated QA state root, and a custom loopback Gateway port (`41103`):

- Natural timer: outbound delivery `1784347997662`, terminal success `1784347997665`.
- Real Gateway `cron.run`: outbound delivery `1784348000474`, terminal success `1784348000476`.
- Both successful one-shots were deleted.

The timestamp ordering is the regression oracle: the old self-block records terminal success before the later asynchronous outbound message; the fixed path delivers first.

## Scope

`next-heartbeat` remains asynchronous by design. Issue #105257 remains open for its intermittent payload-loss report.

---

🤖 AI-assisted: original contributor fix reviewed and rewritten with maintainer tests, changed-gate proof, and live OpenAI Gateway verification.
